key_insight: Reward-wise normalization can still leave uneven batch-level learning because each reward’s advantage energy scales with how often that reward is active across rollout groups.
engineering_relevance: DARA offers a simple batch-adaptive weighting rule that can speed up multi-objective RL training for LLMs without changing the underlying optimization objective.
method: Measure each reward’s advantage energy after GDPO-style normalization.
Estimate active-group density: the fraction of rollout groups where a reward has nonzero relative advantages.
Apply inverse-square-root density correction so rarer active rewards receive more weight.
evidence_signal: On tool calling and mathematical reasoning, DARA reached target behaviors faster than GDPO, with up to 26% fewer training steps for format compliance and up to 65% fewer steps for length compliance.
watch_item: The density-based weights depend on batch statistics, so noisy or small batches may make the correction unstable or less reliable.
paper_title: Make Sparse Rewards Count: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation for Multi-Reward RL
